Hon'ble Rajeev Singh,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A for the State of U.P. and perused the
record.

2. The instant second bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.449
of 2021, under Sections 406, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B, 147, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station -
Gomti Nagar, District - Lucknow, with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that first bail application of the applicant was rejected on 3.3.2023, but till today, trial has not been proceeded.
He further submitted that charge sheet has been filed against the applicant without sending the documents to F.S.L. for examination.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that at the time of deciding the first bail application,
entire relevant record related to the property in question was summoned and examined, wherein it was found that L.D.A. never sold out the property in question to anyone vide sale deed dated 5.5.1994, which was allegedly executed by the officials of the L.D.A. in favour of Pushpa Srivastava,
who was found non-existent, however, the name of Pushpa Srivastava was found in a register, which was prepared by L.D.A. officials in regard to Vishesh Khand, Gomti Nagar, B-Type Plots at Serial No.163. He next submitted that some officials of L.D.A. are behind the sale of the property in question and entered the name of Pushpa Srivastava and others in the record of L.D.A. by making false entries with the intention to grab valuable properties of the L.D.A.

During the course of investigation, the Investigating Officer visited the alleged address of Smt. Pushpa Srivastava, i.e.,
C-45/6, Paper Mill Colony, Balmiki Nagar, Lucknow but he found that in the said house, one Sunita Sonkar was residing, who told that Pushpa Srivastava was never a resident of the said accommodation and she was also not aware about her.

Other neighbours, namely, Alexander s/o Lt.
M.R. Khan, Pravin Gupta s/o Late R.C. Gupta, D.K. Pal and Manoj Kumar Srivastava were also interrogated by the Investigating Officer, who also stated that they were not aware about the alleged Pushpa Srivastava.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that at the time of deciding the first bail application,
Shri Pawan Kumar Gangwar, Secretary, L.D.A. appeared before this Court alongwith original register, in which, the details of B-Type plots of Vishesh Khand, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow were mentioned, in the said register entry in relation to property in question was also found in the name of Smt. Pushpa Srivastava.
6.

The said register, which was perused for the purpose of adjudication of the matter, revealed that same contained 200 pages and every page contains 18 columns, at page No. 82 of the said original register, in column No. 1, the serial number is mentioned as 163.

In column No. 2 of Page No. 82,
the name and address of the allottee is mentioned as Smt. Pushpa Srivastava r/o C-45/6, Paper Mill Colony, Balmiki Nagar, Lucknow.
In column No. 3, the description of plot/house number is mentioned as 3/88.
In column No. 4, the allotment letter and date is mentioned as 3197/88 dated 27.01.1988.
In column No.5, the sale price of the house/plot is mentioned as Rs.55,000/-.
In column No. 6, registration deposit is mentioned as Rs.2500/- and in column No. 7, amount to be recovered in installment is mentioned as 52,500/-.

The aforesaid record further revealed that on 19.04.1988,
19.11.1988 and 10.02.1994, payment of Rs.26,000/- Rs.26,500/- and Rs.5,474/- was made respectively in the accounts of L.D.A.

The original record also reveals that the registry of the said plot was executed on 05.05.1994 and 3 officials of the LDA, i.e., S.O. (P), A.P.O. and J.S. (A) have made signatures on the aforesaid entries.

It was also pointed out that at the time of deciding first bail application this Court also found that on the basis of forged entry in Bahi No. 1, Zild No. 125, Page No. 46, Book No. 172, Page Nos. 553 to 562, Serial No. 10978, the accused persons posed that a sale deed dated 05.05.2000 of the plot in dispute was executed by the LDA in favour of one Raghunath Prasad Kapoor, Cantonment Zone,
Meerut.
Thereafter, the plot in dispute was allegedly sold by Raghunath Prasad Kapoor to Santosh Kumar Yadav.

It was also found that a false entry was made in the registration as well as other record of LDA in relation to the sale deed of Plot No. 3/88, Vishesh Khand, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow Ranjeet Kumar Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ...

2 by the concerned officials of LDA with the association of the co-accused persons, the complaint of which was made to the police, in which, involvement of one Musafir Singh, retired officer of LDA was also found.

Secretary, L.D.A. had also given undertaking before this Court that they will examine the record in consonance with the physical verification of the vacant plots/properties situated at the site and will also take necessary action against the erring officers.

7. Submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that neither the record has been taken into custody by the Investigating Officer nor was sent to the F.S.L. for examination and, in case, there is interpolation in the record of L.D.A. why a single officer of the L.D.A. is not being prosecuted.
It has thus further submitted that applicant, who is in jail since 11.12.2022, may be enlarged on bail.
8. Learned A.G.A. oppose the prayer of the applicant but he did not dispute the fact that in the present case, there is involvement of the officials of L.D.A. and the same is also being investigated.

9. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A., going through the contents of the pleading of the bail application, F.I.R. as well as other relevant documents, including the order dated 3.3.2023 passed by this Court, by which, the first bail application of the applicant was rejected, it is evident that at the time of deciding the first bail application, entire record of L.D.A., as discussed above was summoned and examined, and it was found that if the property was not sold out by the officials of L.D.A., then how the description of sale deed and other details are mentioned in the property register of L.D.A..
It is further evident that there is active involvement of the officials of L.D.A., but all these facts were not examined by the Investigating Officer.

As Pushpa Srivastava was also not traceable, but the Investigating Officer, who was present before this Court stated that now Pushpa Srivastava has admitted that some amount was given by her, but details of the account has not been asked by the Investigating Officer.

10. In such circumstances, the applicant is in jail since 11.12.2022 and the trial is not going on,
therefore, this Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

11. Let applicant - Ranjeet Kumar Yadav - be released on bail in aforesaid Case Crime, on his furnishing personal bond and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not commit or participate in any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

sentences.text: ( iii )
The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(v) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A IPC.
(vi) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

13. However, as there is interpolation in the property register of L.D.A. as discussed above,
therefore, Director, Vigilance U.P. (Establishment), Lucknow is directed to look into the matter and depute a team for detailed inquiry against the erring officials, with whom association, property register of L.D.A. has been interpolated in relation to the plot in question as well as other property and take necessary action.

14. The Bench Secretary of this Court is directed to return the photo copy of the case diary to the learned A.G.A.
15.

Senior Registrar of this Court is directed to communicate copy of this order to the Additional Chief Secretary, Urban Development, Govt. of U.P., Lucknow & Director, Vigilance U.P.
(Establishment), Lucknow, forthwith for action.
